artifacts.summary: Reproduces the 6.9s generate-todo.sh regen cost live, isolates root cause to jq subprocess-spawn count, finds SCOPE_MUTEX_ACQUIRE_BUDGET_MS is hardcoded/non-overridable, and recommends moving regen out of state-write.sh's critical section plus a single-pass jq rewrite and a regression test.

memory_candidates.content: jq subprocess spawn overhead (~2.3ms/call) dominates over file-parse cost for small-to-medium JSON: 1000 spawns of a trivial jq call cost the same wall time as 1000 spawns of the same call on a real ~600KB-derived small string. When optimizing a bash+jq hot loop that calls jq many times per iteration, count subprocess spawns first, not file size.

In task-lock.sh's acquire_named_mutex(), the holder-declared stale_sec (staleness window) is per-call overridable via a CLI argument, but the waiter's own wait_budget_ms (acquire timeout) is NOT — it's hardcoded per named-mutex family (e.g. SCOPE_MUTEX_ACQUIRE_BUDGET_MS=5000 for .scope-lock) with no env-var indirection or CLI override. A caller that only raises stale_sec (to avoid a live-holder being reclaimed) does not thereby raise how long a contending waiter will wait before giving up and ABORTing — these are two independent knobs and only one is exposed.
